minia.name: Multi-agent AI Chief of Staff (Minia)
minia.description: Context was scattered across Gmail, CRM, meetings and documents, multiplied by several companies. An orchestrator agent reachable on Telegram, WhatsApp and Discord, backed by specialised AI staff and a sourced memory where every fact is tied to its evidence. Read-first: any sensitive external write goes through human approval.
minia.problem: Every file started from scratch: context scattered across Gmail, CRM, meetings and documents, forgotten follow-ups, decisions made on incomplete information. All of it multiplied by several companies.
minia.solution: An orchestrator agent reachable on Telegram, WhatsApp and Discord, backed by specialised AI staff and a sourced, versioned memory where every fact is tied to its evidence. Connectors for Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Monday, Sellsy, Fireflies and Pennylane. Read-first: any sensitive external write goes through human approval.

prospection.name: Automated multi-channel prospecting
prospection.description: Automatic lead enrichment, per-channel personalised outreach (email, LinkedIn, phone), automatic ICP targeting.
prospection.problem: Lead generation depended on whatever time the sales team could spare. Manual targeting, generic messaging, follow-ups left to chance.
prospection.solution: Automatic lead enrichment, computed ICP targeting, then per-channel personalised sequences — email, LinkedIn, phone — orchestrated in n8n with AI agents doing the writing.

datahub.name: Data centralisation & AI dashboards
datahub.description: Data warehouse wired to every existing tool, one central management interface, AI-enriched monitoring.
datahub.problem: Data lived in a dozen tools that did not talk to each other. Every business question meant a manual export and a hand-made reconciliation.
datahub.solution: A data warehouse wired to every existing tool, one central management interface, and AI-enriched monitoring that surfaces anomalies before they turn into incidents.

orchestrateur.name: Multi-team Telegram orchestrator
orchestrateur.description: A central Telegram agent coordinating specialised sub-agents — HR, marketing, prospecting, management — without hiring a coordinator.
orchestrateur.problem: Coordinating HR, marketing, prospecting and management called for a full-time coordinator the agency did not want to hire.
orchestrateur.solution: A central Telegram agent routes requests to sub-agents specialised per function, tracks progress and escalates what is stuck. One interface for the founder.

support.name: 24/7 AI customer support
support.description: Conversational agent handling order tracking, returns and FAQ, with smart hand-off to a human.
support.problem: Ticket volume grew with the catalogue. Order tracking, returns and FAQ took up most of an eight-person team's time.
support.solution: A conversational agent on a RAG document base, wired to WhatsApp and Zendesk. It handles routine requests end to end and escalates to a human as soon as the context leaves its scope.

rh.name: HR process automation
rh.description: Full recruiting pipeline: AI CV screening, pre-qualification, interview scheduling and onboarding.
rh.problem: CV screening, pre-qualification and interview logistics ate the HR team's week. Average time-to-hire sat at 45 days.
rh.solution: A fully automated pipeline: NLP CV reading and scoring, asynchronous pre-qualification, interview scheduling in Google Calendar and onboarding triggered in Notion.

stocks.name: Predictive inventory management
stocks.description: AI demand forecasting wired into the ERP, with automatic replenishment and stockout alerts.
stocks.problem: Forecasting ran on Excel, history and gut feel. The result: stockouts on fast movers and overstock on everything else.
stocks.solution: A Python demand-forecasting model wired to the SAP ERP over a real-time API. Replenishment triggered automatically, stockout alerts raised before the shelf empties.

reporting.name: Automated multi-platform reporting
reporting.description: Weekly reports generated automatically by consolidating data from 8 platforms — Shopify, Meta Ads, GA4 and the rest.
reporting.problem: Consolidating figures from eight platforms took two days a week. The report landed after the decision had already been made.
reporting.solution: Automatic collection through each platform's API, consolidation in n8n, formatting and commentary written by GPT-4, published to Notion every Monday morning.

telavie.name: Télavie
telavie.description: Unified telemedicine and healthcare facility management platform, hosted on HDS-certified infrastructure. A coherent system for patients, practitioners and administrators, with real-time exchanges.
telavie.outcome: Telemedicine and administration in a single system
telavie.problem: Healthcare providers juggled a telemedicine tool, a management system and scattered conversations. Nothing talked to anything, and health-data hosting brought its own constraints.
telavie.solution: One platform covering both telemedicine and facility management, with three coherent spaces: patient, practitioner, administrator. Next.js and Prisma on PostgreSQL, client-side data kept fresh with SWR, real-time exchanges over Socket, hosted on HDS-certified infrastructure.

talentfindr.name: TalentFindr
talentfindr.description: AI sourcing platform: search across 800M+ profiles, automatic relevance scoring, verified contact details and multi-channel LinkedIn, email and WhatsApp sequences. Copilot mode, or autopilot with KAIA, the agent that sources, reaches out and follows up on its own. GDPR compliant, hosted in the EU.
talentfindr.outcome: 1,500+ recruiters, agencies and consultancies across 10+ countries
talentfindr.problem: Sourcing is still the most time-consuming part of recruiting: search, verify contact details, write, follow up, then start over on the next role.
talentfindr.solution: An AI sourcing platform across 800M+ profiles: relevance scoring, verified contact details, multi-channel LinkedIn, email and WhatsApp sequences, unified inbox and pipeline management. Two modes: copilot, where the recruiter stays in control, and autopilot with KAIA, the agent that sources, reaches out and follows up on its own. GDPR compliant, hosted in the EU.

growit.name: GrowIt
growit.description: Multi-agent AI prospecting system: autonomous lead identification, extraction and qualification with direct CRM injection.
growit.outcome: From raw lead to CRM with no human step
growit.problem: Identify a target, extract contact details, qualify it, then key it into the CRM: four manual steps repeated on every single lead.
growit.solution: A multi-agent system where each agent owns one step of the chain. The lead comes in raw and lands qualified in the CRM, with no manual pass.

mojo.name: Mojo APP
mojo.description: Intelligent WhatsApp assistant that structures client relations around the clock: conversation management, order taking and schedule organisation.
mojo.outcome: Conversations, orders and calendar run from WhatsApp
mojo.problem: Customer conversations land on WhatsApp at any hour. Orders get lost in the thread, appointments end up noted somewhere else.
mojo.solution: A WhatsApp assistant that holds the conversation, records orders and books appointments in the calendar. The customer keeps their usual channel; the structure happens behind it.

automations.name: +2,000 automations deployed
automations.description: n8n & Make workflows deployed across e-commerce, healthcare, real estate and SaaS. Fewer manual operations, faster growth.
automations.problem: The same picture shows up from one sector to the next: repetitive tasks held together by hand because the tools in place do not talk to each other.
automations.solution: Over 2,000 n8n and Make workflows deployed across e-commerce, healthcare, real estate and SaaS. Connecting the existing tools rather than replacing them, with the same routine: map it, then ship it.

executiveFaq.title: The five questions to answer before deciding

items.question: Why is one place €1,500 excl. VAT when the catalogue price is €4,500?
items.answer: I make an exceptional €3,000 reduction to my fees to create a first documented commercial reference. The scope and delivery standard remain those of the €4,500 excl. VAT Pilot. In exchange, the company agrees to baseline and post-launch measurements, a named testimonial if the result is validated, publication of the case and one future reference call. The place is confirmed once the agreement is signed and a 50% deposit is paid.

items.question: How is ROI measured?
items.answer: Before building, I set a simple baseline with you: time spent, volume processed, errors or delays observed. We review the same indicators after launch. The simulator provides a decision hypothesis; observed figures remain the source of truth.

items.question: Which costs can be added?
items.answer: Subscriptions, API usage and third-party services remain your responsibility. Flow Run is optional. Any expansion to another process, team or custom interface receives a separate priced scope.

items.question: What happens after the 14-day stabilisation period?
items.answer: The system remains documented and is handed over to your team. You can operate it without a subscription to me, or choose Flow Run for monitoring, incidents and an agreed change allowance.

items.question: What happens to my data and access credentials?
items.answer: Access is limited to the agreed scope, and sensitive actions remain subject to your approval. Scoping specifies the data consulted, third-party services used, where data transits and how access is revoked. If these conditions are not acceptable, the project does not start.

problem.title: The problem is not a lack of information. It is having to rebuild the context.
problem.intro: Part of the truth lives in email, another part in the CRM, a meeting note or someone's head. The real cost appears when a decision moves forward without the missing piece.

items.title: Every file starts from scratch
items.body: The history exists, but no one has it in front of them when the decision is made.

items.title: Every tool tells one part
items.body: None of them brings together the decision, its source and the next action.

items.title: Exceptions surface too late
items.body: The process looks healthy until a customer or a team discovers the failure.

items.title: The executive fills the gaps
items.body: You cross-check, chase and arbitrate by hand what the tools fail to coordinate.

examples.title: Start with one useful flow, not a company-wide transformation
examples.intro: The right first scope is narrow, frequent and observable. These are strong starting points for an initial project.

items.title: Prepare a decision brief
items.body: Bring email, documents, CRM records and meeting notes into one sourced brief before a meeting.

items.title: Consolidate reporting
items.body: Collect figures from several tools and flag the gaps that require a decision.

items.title: Surface forgotten actions
items.body: Catch a follow-up, document or approval before it holds the file back.

items.title: Detect a silent failure
items.body: Alert the right person with the relevant context before a customer finds the problem.

path.title: A straightforward way to start small
path.intro: Each step answers one decision. You know what is included, what remains your responsibility and what you keep if you stop there.

steps.title: Qualification call
steps.situation: A process is costing you time or context, but you do not yet know whether it warrants a project.
steps.result: In 30 minutes, the problem, its potential and the appropriate next step become clear — including when the right decision is to build nothing.
steps.scope: One process discussed. No full audit and no written deliverable.

steps.title: Focused scoping
steps.situation: The problem is real, but its mechanics, risks and cost of resolution are still unclear.
steps.result: You leave with a simplified map, the friction and risks, a recommended target, then a scope, timeline and budget you can decide against.
steps.scope: A 90-minute workshop, one process, one organisation, up to three tools or sources, followed by a 30-minute review. Credited if a Flow Pilot or full system starts within 30 days.

steps.title: Flow Pilot
steps.situation: You want to prove value in day-to-day work before extending the system.
steps.result: One useful flow runs in production, documented, monitored and handed over to your team.
steps.scope: One process, one team, up to three sources, one trigger, one main path, its essential exceptions and one output.

steps.title: Full system
steps.situation: One flow has proved itself, or several processes need to share the same context.
steps.result: Your priority tools, approval rules and processes work as one coherent system.
steps.scope: Several processes and tools, sourced memory, permissions, error handling, monitoring, documentation and capability transfer.

steps.title: Flow Run
steps.situation: The system is live and needs to remain reliable as tools, APIs and volumes change.
steps.result: Incidents are detected, corrected and tracked before they become an operational problem.
steps.scope: Monitoring, alerts, fixes and evolution time according to the selected scope.

metrics.label: saved per month, estimated by the executive

guardrails.title: What the system does not decide for you
guardrails.intro: Reliability comes from boundaries as much as automation. These rules are part of the architecture from day one.

items.title: A source before a claim
items.body: Important information must lead back to the email, document or meeting note that supports it.

items.title: Approval before a sensitive action
items.body: AI prepares; you authorise the messages, decisions and external writes that carry consequences.

items.title: A visible exception
items.body: Anything outside the expected path is raised to a person with the relevant context instead of failing silently.

items.title: A system you control
items.body: Accounts, access, rules, documentation and configuration remain transferable and usable.

items.question: Where should I start?
items.answer: Start with the qualification call if you have a specific process in mind. If it needs to be clarified before development, focused scoping is the next step. The Pilot fits when the scope and expected outcome are already clear enough.

items.question: What do I receive from focused scoping?
items.answer: A simplified map of the current process, its friction, risks and dependencies, a recommended target flow, then an estimate of scope, timeline and budget. The document remains useful if you decide not to continue with me.

items.question: Is the €290 scoping fee added to the Pilot price?
items.answer: No. If the Pilot starts within 30 days, the €290 already paid is credited against the remaining amount. This credit also applies to the single Founding Partner place.

items.question: Why are the Pilot and the full system priced differently?
items.answer: They do not cover the same scope. The Pilot puts one flow into production to prove its value. A full system connects several processes, tools, permissions and monitoring mechanisms. The Pilot is a standalone product.

items.question: Can the AI write or act without approval?
items.answer: Sensitive external actions wait for human approval. The system can gather, verify, prepare and suggest; the decision and final authorisation remain yours.

items.question: How long does it take to go live?
items.answer: Focused scoping is delivered within five business days of the workshop. A Flow Pilot typically takes two to three weeks once access and approvals are available. A full system timeline is fixed with its scope.

items.question: What happens after delivery?
items.answer: The system is documented and handed over to your team. The Pilot includes a corrective stabilisation period. If you want continuous monitoring and evolution, Flow Run can take over afterwards.

items.question: How are data and access handled?
items.answer: The required tools, accounts, data and access levels are agreed before work starts. The system receives only the permissions needed for the scope, and sensitive actions remain subject to your approval rules.

items.question: Is full operational mapping required?
items.answer: No. It is useful when several flows need to be studied or when you want a broader operational view. For one priority process that is already identified, focused scoping or a Pilot is usually more proportionate.

final.title: Bring one process and three figures. Leave with a decision.
final.body: Monthly volume, time spent and loaded cost are enough for a first calculation. In 30 minutes, I test with you whether the potential gain justifies scoping or a Pilot.
final.note: Free qualification call. No hidden audit and no commitment to continue.

meta.title: AI automation services for SMEs | Annaël Lalason
meta.description: Process automation, human-approved AI agents and custom systems architecture for SMEs and growing teams.

hero.title: Turn one manual process into an operational system.
hero.body: I map the real work, connect the tools already in place and deliver a measurable workflow your team can operate. Not an isolated demo: a documented, monitored and transferable production system.
hero.note: One point of contact · one metric before building · human approval for sensitive actions

proof.title: Technology matters. A usable outcome matters more.
proof.body: Every engagement starts with observable friction and ends with a system the team can monitor, correct and hand over.

catalog.title: Choose the level that fits the problem, not the fashionable tool.
catalog.intro: A precise process may need targeted automation. Scattered context may justify an AI agent. Several interdependent workflows need architecture first.

items.title: Process automation
items.for: Your team re-enters, consolidates, follows up or checks the same information every week.
items.outcome: Remove repetitive steps without replacing tools that already work.
items.body: I connect your applications through APIs, n8n or Make, then add the controls and alerts required for the workflow to hold up in production.

items.title: Human-approved AI agents
items.for: Decisions take too long because context is scattered across messages, documents and business tools.
items.outcome: Prepare the right information and next action without blindly delegating the decision.
items.body: The agent gathers sources, prepares an answer or action, and asks for approval whenever the company is committed. Every important claim remains tied to its evidence.

items.title: Systems and product architecture
items.for: Several processes, datasets and roles need to work together in one coherent interface.
items.outcome: Move from a pile of tools to a maintainable, secure and scalable system.
items.body: I design the architecture, data flows, permissions and interface before orchestrating delivery of an application or complete system.

approach.title: Measure before you automate.
approach.body: The goal is not to build the most impressive system. It is to solve the right problem with a scope the team can adopt.

steps.title: Observe
steps.body: Volume, time spent, errors, delays and people involved become the decision baseline.

steps.title: Scope
steps.body: We choose one outcome, one main path, the essential exceptions and explicit boundaries.

steps.title: Ship
steps.body: The workflow is connected, tested and launched with logs and alerts.

steps.title: Stabilise
steps.body: The team uses the system, gaps are corrected and the documentation is handed over.

qualification.title: Is this the right time to automate?
qualification.body: Good automation starts with a process frequent enough to measure and stable enough to scope.
qualification.fitsTitle: The project is probably ready if
fits: A business owner can explain the current process
Volume, time or errors can be estimated
The relevant tools provide the required access
limits: The process still changes every week
Nobody can approve rules and exceptions
The goal is simply to add AI without a specific business outcome

final.title: Start with one process, not a company-wide transformation.
final.body: In 30 minutes, we check volume, friction and potential value. If the case is not strong enough, I will say so before any paid scoping.

meta.title: AI, automation and product case studies | Annaël Lalason
meta.description: Explore production AI systems, automations and products: context, architecture, observed outcomes and limitations.

hero.title: Systems shipped. Outcomes kept in context.
hero.body: Each case explains the starting problem, the system delivered and the outcomes available. Figures include their scope so evidence remains distinct from a promise.

minia.metaTitle: Minia: multi-agent AI Chief of Staff | Case study
minia.metaDescription: How a multi-company executive centralised context with an AI Chief of Staff, 21 automations and more than 6 specialised agents.
minia.lesson: A useful agent does more than answer questions. It retrieves the source, separates knowledge from assumptions and waits for approval before sensitive external writes.
minia.readingNote: The 35–50 monthly hours are the executive's estimate for a broader system. They are an observed reference, not a guarantee for another context.

reporting.metaTitle: Automated reporting: from 2 days to 15 minutes | Case study
reporting.metaDescription: Case study of e-commerce reporting across eight platforms, published every Monday through n8n, Notion and GPT-4.
reporting.lesson: The value comes from more than automatic collection. It requires shared metric definitions, a stable publishing time and an alert when a source is missing.
reporting.readingNote: The outcomes apply to the scope described and depend on API availability, data quality and stable business definitions.

telavie.metaTitle: Télavie: unified telemedicine platform | Case study
telavie.metaDescription: Architecture of a telemedicine platform unifying patients, practitioners and administrators with Next.js, PostgreSQL and HDS hosting.
telavie.lesson: In a healthcare product, user experience and role architecture must be designed together: every screen depends on permissions, data and the care journey.
telavie.readingNote: The evidence describes the platform's functional and technical scope. It is not a measure of medical outcomes.

talentfindr.metaTitle: TalentFindr: AI sourcing platform | Case study
talentfindr.metaDescription: Case study of an AI sourcing platform covering more than 800 million profiles, with scoring and multi-channel sequences.
talentfindr.lesson: A sourcing agent's autonomy depends less on message generation than on targeting quality, sequence rules and the visibility retained by the recruiter.
talentfindr.readingNote: Profile, user and country figures describe the platform's stated reach. They do not by themselves represent a recruiting outcome.

final.title: Your case does not need to look like these.
final.body: It simply needs observable friction, an accountable owner and an outcome the team will recognise.
